turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I finally fixed that annoying bug in the auth middleware. It was a race condition in the token refresh logic.
Great to hear you got that sorted out. Race conditions in auth flows can be tricky to reproduce. Did you add a test case for it?
Yes, I did. Anyway, I've been reading up on Generative UI again. I'm trying to figure out how the UX agent learns.
That's an interesting area. Are you looking at specific libraries or frameworks?
No, just general architecture. I noticed that the mechanism for teaching the UX agent templates and hierarchy (prompt-rules, retrieval, or post-processing) is unspecified.
Ah, that makes sense. Many papers leave that implementation detail vague or open-ended.
Exactly. It leaves a lot to the imagination. Oh, did you check if my hardware order shipped yet?
Let me check... Yes, it says it shipped yesterday. Should arrive by Friday.
Lloyd, the weather is supposed to rain all weekend. I think I'll stay in and cook.
Good plan. Do you have a recipe in mind, or do you want suggestions?
I'll make pasta. It's easy. Speaking of easy, I had a breakthrough on the Generative UI streaming concept.
I realized that Generative UI allows agents to stream UI definitions (JSON or Python) which are rendered in real-time by the server.
That sounds much more efficient than waiting for the full response. Real-time rendering definitely improves UX.
Yeah, it cuts down latency significantly. I need to prototype this soon.
Let me know if you need help setting up the server-side renderer.
